editorial:
Imagine living in a quiet beach town where nothing ever happens, only to have your world flipped upside down in one afternoon. You follow Andy, a 12-year-old kid who accidentally sees a brutal attack. Instead of feeling safe, he starts to feel like the whole town is watching him and closing in. The movie captures that scary feeling of being a kid and realizing that the adults around you aren't always the good guys. It feels heavy and tense, making you worry for Andy every time he turns a corner.

What really works here is the acting, especially the young lead who makes you feel his panic. The pacing is slow at first, but it builds up to a point where you can't look away. Some parts might feel a bit too quiet for people who want non-stop action, but if you like slow-burn mysteries, you will love it. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend.
endingExplained: At the end, the tension finally breaks when the truth about the attack comes out. You see that the people Andy trusted were actually involved in the violence he witnessed. Andy has to face his fears in a final confrontation to survive. He eventually finds a way to escape the cycle of violence, but the movie leaves you feeling that he has lost his childhood innocence forever. It wraps up with a sad but honest look at trauma.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological thrillers and stories about coming of age in dark settings.
